samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one thin grey trail: a single line of constant width that zigzags along but never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself. One end of the trail carries a solid black round bead and the other end carries a solid black square block. The walk starts at the round bead and follows the trail all the way to the square block. Small coloured triangles sit directly on the trail, each coloured red, green, blue or purple. A triangle whose point aims upwards adds one to a running count, and a triangle whose point aims downwards takes one away from it. The count is zero at the bead, it changes only when the walk meets a triangle, and it is allowed to fall below zero. Exactly one triangle on the trail is the place where the running count reaches its highest value. Only the order of the triangles along the trail matters, not how far apart they are and not where they sit on the canvas. The trail may lie anywhere in the picture, and every pale grey shape lying off the trail is inert decoration. What colour is the triangle at which the running count reaches its highest value? Answer with one of red, green, blue or purple.
